description: Complete scripted analysis of fixtures/repos/mini-app: two perspectives, nested groups, evidence for every element and relationship, coverage report.

args.content:
graph LR
    http-api["HTTP API\nsrc/server.ts, src/routes/"]
    order-service["Order Service\nsrc/services/"]
    database["Database\nsrc/db/"]
    payment-gateway["Payment Gateway\nsrc/integrations/payment-gateway.ts"]
    configuration["Configuration\nsrc/config.ts"]
    http-api -->|"place and fetch orders"| order-service
    order-service -->|"persist and load orders"| database
    order-service -->|"charge the customer"| payment-gateway
    http-api -->|"reads settings at start-up"| configuration
    classDef entry fill:#89b4fa,stroke:#89b4fa,color:#1e1e2e
    classDef store fill:#a6e3a1,stroke:#a6e3a1,color:#1e1e2e
    classDef external fill:#585b70,stroke:#585b70,color:#cdd6f4
    class http-api entry
    class database store
    class payment-gateway external
A small order service: an Express HTTP API accepts orders, an order service prices them and charges the customer through an external payment gateway, and a PostgreSQL client stores the result.
Single Node.js process. Configuration comes from environment variables read once at start-up.

args.claim: The service is a single Express application that wires a database, a payment gateway and an order service together at start-up.

args.content: HTTP entry point. src/server.ts builds the Express app, mounts the /orders router and a /health endpoint, and starts listening on the configured port.

graph LR
    server-bootstrap["Server Bootstrap\nsrc/server.ts"]
    order-routes["Order Routes\nsrc/routes/orders.ts"]
    server-bootstrap -->|"mounts the /orders router"| order-routes

args.claim: src/server.ts is the process entry point: it creates the Express app and starts listening.
The bootstrap mounts the order router under /orders.

args.content: Loads configuration, creates the database client, payment gateway and order service, builds the Express app and starts listening.

args.claim: Dependencies are constructed once in src/server.ts and passed to the routes by argument.

args.content: Express router for POST /orders (validates the body, places an order) and GET /orders/:id (returns an order or 404).
Request bodies are only checked for presence; item fields are not validated before pricing.

args.claim: POST /orders checks customerId and a non-empty items array before calling the order service.
Item contents are not validated beyond being an array.
Route handlers call placeOrder and getOrder on the order service.
The bootstrap calls loadConfig once with process.env.

args.content: Business logic for orders: prices an order, charges the customer, and records the outcome.

graph LR
    order-orchestration["Order Orchestration\nsrc/services/order-service.ts"]
    pricing-rules["Pricing Rules\nsrc/services/pricing.ts"]
    order-orchestration -->|"computes totals"| pricing-rules

args.claim: The order service composes pricing, the payment gateway and the database client.
placeOrder calls priceOrder to compute the total.

args.content: placeOrder prices the order, charges the gateway, stores the order with status paid or payment_failed; getOrder reads an order by id.
The charge happens before the order is stored; a failure between the two steps would charge without a record.

args.claim: Payment is requested before the order row is inserted.

args.content: Pure function priceOrder: 5% discount on lines above 10 units, then a flat 8% tax.

args.claim: Pricing applies a 5% bulk discount above 10 units per line and 8% tax.
The order service inserts and finds orders through the Db interface.
placeOrder charges the customer through the gateway before storing.

args.content: PostgreSQL access: a pooled client and the SQL statements it runs.

graph LR
    db-client["DB Client\nsrc/db/client.ts"]
    order-queries["Order Queries\nsrc/db/queries.ts"]
    db-client -->|"runs SQL text"| order-queries

args.claim: The database layer is a pg Pool wrapped by a small Db interface.
The client imports its two statements from queries.ts.

args.content: createDb builds a pg Pool (max 5 connections) and exposes insertOrder and findOrder.

args.claim: The pool is limited to five connections.

args.content: Two parameterised SQL statements for inserting and selecting an order.

args.claim: Both statements use positional parameters.

args.content: External payment provider reached over HTTPS: charge posts to /v1/charges with a bearer API key and reports approved or not.
A non-2xx response is treated as a declined payment and no error detail is kept.

args.claim: Charges are POSTed to the provider with a bearer token.

args.content: loadConfig reads port, database URL and payment API settings from environment variables with defaults.

args.claim: All settings come from environment variables with local defaults.

args.content:
graph LR
    route-handler["Route Handler\nsrc/routes/orders.ts"]
    pricing["Pricing\nsrc/services/pricing.ts"]
    charge-payment["Charge Payment\nsrc/integrations/payment-gateway.ts"]
    persist-order["Persist Order\nsrc/db/client.ts"]
    route-handler -->|"items from the request body"| pricing
    pricing -->|"total in cents"| charge-payment
    charge-payment -->|"approved flag decides the status"| persist-order
    classDef entry fill:#89b4fa,stroke:#89b4fa,color:#1e1e2e
    class route-handler entry
How POST /orders is handled end to end: validate, price, charge, store, respond with 201.

args.claim: POST /orders flows route handler, order service, pricing, payment gateway and database in that order.

args.content: Validates the body and calls placeOrder; responds 400 on a bad body and 201 with the order otherwise.

args.claim: The handler answers 400 for a missing customerId or empty items.

args.content: priceOrder returns subtotal, tax and total in cents.

args.claim: priceOrder returns subtotalCents, taxCents and totalCents.

args.content: The gateway charge call; a declined or failed charge yields approved: false.

args.claim: A non-ok HTTP response maps to approved: false.

args.content: insertOrder stores the order with status paid or payment_failed and returns its id.

args.claim: The returned row id is used as the order id.
The handler passes items through placeOrder, which prices them.
placeOrder charges price.totalCents.
The approved flag selects paid or payment_failed before insert.

args.notes: All ten files of the repository were read; both perspectives cover the full request path.
